strategies.name: Detection Strategy for Event Triggered Execution via Trap (T1546.005)

analytics.name: Analytic 1038
analytics.guidance: Correlate file modifications in shell startup scripts (e.g., .bashrc, .profile) with embedded `trap` commands and observe if those changes are followed by the unexpected execution of child processes when terminal signals (e.g., SIGINT) are triggered. Use contextual linking with user session activity to detect privilege misuse.

tuning.description: The path to user profile scripts (e.g., ~/.bashrc, ~/.zshrc); may differ by distro or shell type.
Trap signal (e.g., INT, HUP, TERM) can be environment-specific or attacker-tuned to evade.
Temporal threshold to correlate trap insertion and process execution (e.g., 10s-5min)

log_sources.name: auditd:SYSCALL
log_sources.channel: Modification of user shell profile or trap registration via echo/redirection (e.g., echo "trap 'malicious_cmd' INT" >> ~/.bashrc)

analytics.name: Analytic 1039
analytics.guidance: Detect unauthorized `trap` command registrations in shell startup files (e.g., .zprofile, .bash_profile, .zshrc) followed by execution chains during user terminal interaction. Use Unified Logs and EDR telemetry to correlate shell command parsing and process tree anomalies.

tuning.description: Startup files vary by shell (.bash_profile, .zshrc, etc.)
Short benign traps may differ from longer/multi-command malicious traps
Score or detect if new child process deviates from shell’s typical behavior

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: Command line containing `trap` or `echo 'trap` written to login shell files

log_sources.name: macos:unifiedlog
log_sources.channel: File write or append to .zshrc, .bash_profile, .zprofile, etc.
